A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same entropic time scheduling work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original one-dimensional KL-divergence simulations and image-generation evaluations using FID and FD-DINOv2 in Section 6 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 retains those original simulation and image-generation results and adds qualitative image comparisons in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The scalar estimator pseudocode changes from drawing data separately at each timestep in v3 Algorithm 1 to reusing one batch in v4 Algorithm 2. The scheduling definitions, spectral estimator, and diffusion models remain unchanged; the added integration and sampling pseudocode otherwise documents existing operations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate discrete point mixtures, Gaussian mixtures, CIFAR10, FFHQ, and ImageNet at 64 and 512 resolution. Medical imaging, audio, text, and distillation remain proposed applications rather than added evaluations.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same standard-time/EDM comparisons against entropic, rescaled, and applicable spectral-rescaled schedules. No newly cited work becomes an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The scalar calibration pseudocode now specifies a shared data batch across timesteps instead of per-timestep resampling. Appendix H otherwise retains the model configurations, 50,000-image evaluations, NFE budgets, metrics, and 128 calibration times with 1,024 samples per time. This does not establish that benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds further qualitative NFE comparisons in Figure 7 and deterministic-DDIM schedule comparisons in Figures 13–15. Existing toy-distribution analyses, calibration sensitivity checks, and the non-rescaled entropy failure example are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 repetitions for the toy KL estimates and a single run for image metrics. The new checklist repeats the existing single-run disclosure without adding uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: All six numerical tables and the KL plots are unchanged. Figure 2 reverses the displayed relative ordering of rescaled and spectral-rescaled curves around time 10, beyond changing the axis scale. v4 also adds generated-image examples in Figures 7 and 13–15.

T1.justification: v4 corrects the Fokker–Planck coefficient in Equation 2 from g(t) to g(t)^2/2 and corrects sigma(tau)=tau in Appendix E. It adds the integrated entropy identity in Equation 14 and its claimed variational-bound connection; the identity's boundary assumptions are unstated. The principal invariance and optimality proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the principal invariance and inference-quality claims. Section 7 newly highlights the variational-objective connection and proposes entropic time for training and distillation, extending potential applicability without claiming demonstrated training results.

C2.justification: Section 7 removes the explicit characterization of spectral weighting as heuristic and the call for optimal anisotropic reweighting. It adds explanations of potential training and distillation uses. Section 5.4 still acknowledges the anisotropic issue, and the higher-order-solver limitation remains.

D1.justification: v4 announces an author code repository and supplies explicit inverse-time interpolation and cumulative entropy-integration pseudocode. It also annotates the retained spectral estimator. These improve implementation documentation, although repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds Franzese et al. (2025) and Kingma et al. (2021), acknowledges similar information-theoretic equations in prior work, and connects its formulation to variational diffusion. The broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 revises selected explanations in Sections 4–5 and substantially rewrites the short future-work discussion. It reorganizes algorithm documentation, adds a NeurIPS checklist, and updates affiliations and the venue header while retaining the overall section structure.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adopts logarithmic time and revised axis, colorbar, and legend presentation. v4 adds Figures 7 and 13–15 and reflows retained figures, tables, and algorithm displays. Most existing visual content is preserved.

improvement.justification: v4 improves implementation documentation and corrects Equation 2. However, its new Equation 14 lacks boundary assumptions reconciling integration from zero with Section 5.3's continuous-entropy divergence, and Section 7 removes an explicit heuristic-weighting caveat. With the numerical benchmark evidence unchanged, these benefits and unresolved theoretical qualifications prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
